answer: Each applicant locks a 70-credit bond and registers one trellis frame of timber, on a rig whose quartz clock times the load hold. An auditor recomputes deflection from the load table and timber span table; a deflection beyond tolerance, reused trellis key, or copied load log burns the bond. The first filing costs 41 credits, the kth costs 41+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6035 and 1000 fakes pay 3,038,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A rented-frame ring fails because a reused key and quartz timestamps expose the second claim. An honest operator pays 41 once and reclaims the bond after audit.
